editor_note: Entry 85 is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the contrast between "계정 수준에서 부여할 수 있는 항목" (GET /accounts/{id}) and "특정 인스턴스에 이미 부여된 항목" (GET /functions), and "부여 가능한 유효한 값을 알아보고 … 결과를 확인하세요" matches the English's discover-then-confirm split without drifting.

All three rewritten entries (4, 5, 7) match the English line for line. The heading is 'IBM Quantum 컴퓨팅 서비스', the column header is '이 권한이 필요한 작업', and every row maps correctly, e.g. 'Run a job' is '작업 실행', 'Close job session' is '작업 Session 닫기' and 'Get Job by ID' is 'ID로 작업 가져오기'. No permission-to-action pairing is swapped or dropped.

All three rewritten entries (7, 20, 34) keep the English meaning. Nothing drifts or is invented. Entry 34 says "회로를 Transpile하고" for circuit, but every other entry in the file uses "Circuit", including the same sentence. Entry 34 also has the calque "원래 [양자 볼륨 논문]", which reads better as "원 논문". Entry 20's "파라미터를 `0`으로 할당합니다" is slightly unnatural; "`0`을 할당합니다" or "`0`으로 설정합니다" is more idiomatic.

examples.source: the software stack transpiling and post-processing results
examples.translation: 회로를 Transpile하고 결과를 후처리하는 소프트웨어 스택
examples.suggested: Circuit을 Transpile하고 결과를 후처리하는 소프트웨어 스택
examples.why: '회로' appears only here. Every other entry, including this same sentence, renders circuit as 'Circuit'.

examples.source: Read more about quantum volume in the original [quantum volume paper]
examples.translation: 양자 볼륨에 대한 자세한 내용은 원래 [양자 볼륨 논문]을 참조하세요.
examples.suggested: 양자 볼륨에 대한 자세한 내용은 [양자 볼륨 원 논문]을 참조하세요.
examples.why: '원래 논문' is a literal calque of 'original paper'. Korean technical writing uses '원 논문' or '최초 논문'.

examples.source: the following code cell assigns each parameter in the circuit to `0`.
examples.translation: 다음 코드 셀은 Circuit의 각 파라미터를 `0`으로 할당합니다.
examples.suggested: 다음 코드 셀은 Circuit의 각 파라미터에 `0`을 할당합니다.
examples.why: Korean says '~에 값을 할당하다' ('assign a value to ~'), not '~를 0으로 할당하다'. The current sentence copies the English syntax.

editor_note: None of the 36 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Conditions and caveats are all kept, including sign-in above four qubits (32), catalog versus circuit deletion (66-67), ungrouping possibly changing execution order (62), and a reduced purity range of [0.5, 1] (147). What's left is polish. Entry 121 translates the UI label "Visualizations seed" as "시각화 시드" and the Edit menu as "편집 메뉴", but the rest of the page keeps UI labels in English (Info, Paste, Run circuit, Group). Entry 32 adds a parenthetical "(5개 이상의)" that isn't in the English. Entry 145 splits the explanation into two back-to-back "…때문입니다" sentences, so the entanglement reason no longer attaches to the N-probabilities point. Entry 38's link-text phrasing "연산 추가하거나 … 입력을 사용할 수 있습니다" is ungrammatical.

examples.source: You can see the seed number by selecting "Visualizations seed" from the Edit menu.
examples.translation: 편집 메뉴에서 "시각화 시드"를 선택하면 시드 번호를 확인할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: Edit 메뉴에서 "Visualizations seed"를 선택하면 시드 번호를 확인할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The UI label is translated here, but the rest of the page keeps UI labels in English (Info, Paste, Run circuit). A learner looking for '시각화 시드' in the English-only Composer UI won't find it.

examples.source: as N-qubit phase disks would only contain $N$ probabilities and $N$ phases; this is because most states are entangled and are not separable
examples.translation: N-Qubit 위상 디스크는 $N$개의 확률과 $N$개의 위상만 포함하기 때문입니다. 대부분의 상태는 얽혀 있어 … 분리할 수 없기 때문입니다.
examples.suggested: N-Qubit 위상 디스크에는 $N$개의 확률과 $N$개의 위상만 담기기 때문인데, 이는 대부분의 상태가 얽혀 있어 독립적인 단일 Qubit 상태로 분리할 수 없기 때문입니다.
examples.why: Two back-to-back '…때문입니다' sentences read as machine translation and cut the causal link the English makes.

examples.source: if you want to visualize a circuit that has more than four qubits
examples.translation: 4개를 초과하는(5개 이상의) Qubit을 가진 Circuit을 시각화하려면
examples.suggested: Qubit이 4개보다 많은 Circuit을 시각화하려면
examples.why: The parenthetical is redundant and isn't in the English. It's correct but clunky.

examples.source: you can either [drag and drop operations](...), or you can enter [OpenQASM code](...) into the code editor.
examples.translation: [드래그 앤 드롭으로 연산 추가](...)하거나, 코드 편집기에 [OpenQASM 코드 입력](...)을 사용할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: [연산을 드래그 앤 드롭](...)하거나, 코드 편집기에 [OpenQASM 코드](...)를 입력할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The link text's noun phrases don't fit the sentence, so '연산 추가하거나' is missing its object particle and '입력을 사용할' is a calque.

editor_note: The eight rewritten entries keep the English meaning and use terms consistently with the rest of the page, such as 행렬 곱 상태(matrix product state), 기본 오류 완화 옵션이 적용된 EstimatorV2, 깊이가 줄어든 Circuit and 2-Qubit 깊이, all in natural 해요체.

All four rewritten entries (4, 5, 6, 27) keep the source meaning. The error-mitigation list, the v0.50.0 client-side primitives note, the 'drop-in replacement, only the import changes' claim with its 'largely' qualifier (대부분), and the recommendation list all match the English. The one slip is in entry 27: it writes 'Primitives를 연習하세요' with an English plural -s, while every other entry on the page uses the bare 'Primitive'. A native editor would change it to 'Primitive를' to stay consistent.

examples.source: Practice with primitives by working through the [Cost function lesson]...
examples.translation: IBM Quantum Learning의 [비용 함수 강의](...)를 통해 Primitives를 연습하세요.
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Learning의 [비용 함수 강의](...)를 통해 Primitive를 연습해 보세요.
examples.why: Korean does not add an English plural -s to a kept English term. Every other entry on the page uses 'Primitive', so 'Primitives' is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Entries 25 and 26 are faithful. They keep the "제한됨"/"남은 양" labels and the "28일 롤링 사용 윈도우" wording from entries 13 and 20, and the pending-vs-active split ("대기 중인 워크로드는 … 대기열에 남아 있지만 … 활성 워크로드는 계속 실행됩니다"), the "세션 모드" caveat and the hedge "가능성이 있습니다" all match the English.

Entry 22 keeps the English meaning. The hedges are intact ("달라질 수 있습니다", "경우에 따라", "달성할 수 있습니다"), and the caveat that classical and quantum samples can reach similar quality after equivalent post-processing is not weakened or inverted. There are two small consistency slips. "workflow" is written 워크플로우 here but 워크플로 everywhere else on the page (entries 10, 17, 18). "solution quality" is 해 품질 here but 솔루션 품질 in entry 14. The entry also uses 합니다체 rather than the 해요체 convention, although most of the surrounding page is written the same way.

examples.line_approx: Evaluation should therefore consider the complete optimization workflow.
examples.source: the complete optimization workflow
examples.translation: 전체 최적화 워크플로우를 고려해야 합니다
examples.suggested: 전체 최적화 워크플로를 고려해야 해요
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page it is 워크플로 (entries 10, 17, 18). This entry also uses 합니다체 instead of the 해요체 convention.

examples.line_approx: might achieve similar final solution quality after equivalent post-processing
examples.source: similar final solution quality
examples.translation: 유사한 최종 해 품질
examples.suggested: 유사한 최종 솔루션 품질
examples.why: Entry 14 translates "solution quality" as 솔루션 품질, and the page uses 솔루션 for "solution" throughout. Both terms are clear, so this is a consistency slip and does not mislead.

editor_note: In both rewritten headings, "breaking package changes" became "주요 패키지 변경 사항" ("major package changes"). That drops the "breaks compatibility" sense of "breaking". It does not mislead, because the caution admonition in [4] and the prose in [3] still say that environments will break. The rendering also matches the page's existing use of 주요 for "breaking" in [5] and [6]. A native editor would still make the heading say the change breaks compatibility, e.g. "호환성을 깨는 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기". Ideally [5] and [6] would be aligned the same way.

examples.source: Understand the breaking package changes
examples.translation: 주요 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기
examples.suggested: 호환성을 깨는 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기
examples.why: 'breaking' means the change breaks backward compatibility, but 주요 only means 'major/main'. It softens the warning, though the body text still conveys it.

examples.source: Understand the breaking package changes {#understand-the-breaking-package-changes}
examples.translation: 주요 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기 {#understand-the-breaking-package-changes}
examples.suggested: 호환성을 깨는 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기 {#understand-the-breaking-package-changes}
examples.why: Same heading and the same softening of 'breaking'. It should be fixed together with entry 1 and, ideally, 주요 in [5] and [6].

editor_note: Entry 5 drops its subject. The English tells the reader to use "IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing, a platform service" to route events. The Korean only says "you can route audit events…" and never says which service does the routing or that it is a separate platform service. A learner could assume routing is built into IBM Quantum System Service. Entry 6 then refers to Activity Tracker Event Routing as if the reader already knows it. In entry 10, "Action" and "job" are both rendered 작업, so the header reads "작업 | 트리거하는 작업". That header is confusing and should say something like "이벤트 작업 | 트리거 요청". Entry 3 is faithful.

examples.source: You can use IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing, a platform service, to route auditing events in your account to destinations of your choice by configuring targets and routes...
examples.translation: 활동 추적 이벤트가 전송될 위치를 정의하는 대상과 경로를 구성해, 계정의 감사 이벤트를 원하는 목적지로 라우팅할 수 있어요.
examples.suggested: 플랫폼 서비스인 IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing을 사용하면, 활동 추적 이벤트가 전송될 위치를 정의하는 대상과 경로를 구성해 계정의 감사 이벤트를 원하는 목적지로 라우팅할 수 있어요.
examples.why: The Korean leaves out the service that does the routing, which is the whole point of the English sentence. Readers are no longer told which tool to use, and entry 6 then mentions that tool without it ever being introduced.

examples.source: | Action | Triggered by |
examples.translation: | 작업 | 트리거하는 작업 |
examples.suggested: | 이벤트 작업(Action) | 트리거 요청 |
examples.why: 작업 is used both for the event action and for 'job' in the rows (작업 취소, 작업 실행). That makes the header read as 'job | the job that triggers', which is ambiguous and reads like a calque.

examples.source: Cancel a job / Run a job / Get jobs
examples.translation: 작업 취소 / 작업 실행 / 작업 목록 가져오기
examples.suggested: Change the column header so it no longer uses 작업 (as in the example above), so that 작업 in these rows clearly means a job.
examples.why: Using the same word in the header and in the rows blurs the difference between an audit action and a quantum job.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Nothing is inverted or dropped: statevector 계산, 샘플링 오버헤드(일명 "샷 노이즈"), the shot order the bitstrings keep, and "Exact and noisy simulation" → "정확한 시뮬레이션 및 노이즈 시뮬레이션" all match. Two English calques remain. In entries 26 and 43, "introduce the effect … can be modified" becomes "효과를 도입하도록 수정할 수 있습니다", which reads as machine translation. In entry 43, "accepts a `shots` argument" becomes "`shots` 인수를 허용합니다", but a Korean writer would say the interface "받습니다" an argument. These entries use the -습니다 style rather than 해요체. The rest of the page does the same, so I did not flag it as a slip.

examples.source: However, this can be modified to introduce the effect of the sampling overhead (also known as "shot noise").
examples.translation: 그러나 샘플링 오버헤드(일명 "샷 노이즈")의 효과를 도입하도록 수정할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 그러나 샘플링 오버헤드(일명 "샷 노이즈")의 효과가 반영되도록 설정을 바꿀 수도 있습니다.
examples.why: '효과를 도입하도록 수정' copies the English word for word. Korean technical writing says the effect gets '반영' (reflected), not '도입' (introduced).

examples.source: the Sampler interface accepts a `shots` argument that can be defined at the PUB level.
examples.translation: Sampler 인터페이스는 PUB 수준에서 정의할 수 있는 `shots` 인수를 허용합니다.
examples.suggested: Sampler 인터페이스는 PUB 수준에서 지정할 수 있는 `shots` 인수를 받습니다.
examples.why: '인수를 허용합니다' is a machine-translation calque of 'accepts an argument'. Korean API docs say '인수를 받습니다'.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The classical-control mapping in [15] (0 means not applied, 1 means applied) and the Z/X/ZX corrections in [48]/[53]/[58] are all faithful. Entry [83] has the most slips. It drops "one day" and "perhaps", renders "a process known as" as the calque "한 가지 알려진 프로세스인", and uses the nonstandard "불완벽한" where "불완전한" is standard. In [37], "마법 같은 일이 일어났을 수도 있습니다" loses the "look like" hedge from the English. Entries [62] and [83] each switch into 해요체 ("얻어요", "점이에요") partway through a paragraph otherwise in 합니다체, so the register is uneven.

examples.source: it is reasonable to speculate that teleportation could one day become a standard way ... perhaps through a process known as *entanglement distillation*
examples.translation: 텔레포테이션이 한 가지 알려진 프로세스인 *얽힘 정제*를 통해 양자 정보를 통신하는 표준 방식이 될 수 있다고 추측하는 것이 합리적입니다.
examples.suggested: 텔레포테이션이 언젠가는, 아마도 *얽힘 정제*라고 알려진 과정을 통해, 양자 정보를 통신하는 표준 방식이 될 수 있다고 추측해 볼 만합니다.
examples.why: 'one day' and 'perhaps' are dropped, which makes the speculation a little stronger than the English. 'a process known as' is calqued as 'one known process'.

examples.source: noisy (or imperfect) e-bits
examples.translation: 잡음이 있는(또는 불완벽한) e-bit
examples.suggested: 잡음이 있는(또는 불완전한) e-bit
examples.why: '불완벽한' is nonstandard Korean. The usual word for 'imperfect' is '불완전한'.

examples.source: At first glance, it might look like something magical has happened
examples.translation: 언뜻 보면 마법 같은 일이 일어났을 수도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 언뜻 보면 마법 같은 일이 일어난 것처럼 보일 수도 있습니다.
examples.why: The Korean says something magical 'may have happened' rather than 'might look like' it happened. The next sentence calls it an illusion, so the 'appears' hedge should be kept.

examples.source: Notice that Alice's measurements yield absolutely no information ... here Bob obtains the state without it being disturbed.
examples.translation: ...절대적으로 정보를 제공하지 않습니다. ... Bob이 교란되지 않은 상태를 그대로 얻어요.
examples.suggested: ...에 대해 아무런 정보도 주지 않는다는 점에 주목하세요. ... Bob은 교란되지 않은 상태를 그대로 얻습니다.
examples.why: '절대적으로 ... 않습니다' is a calque; '전혀/아무런' is more natural. The imperative 'Notice' is dropped. The last sentence switches to 해요체 in a 합니다체 paragraph.

examples.source: (which we will commonly do when it is convenient)
examples.translation: (편리할 때 일반적으로 수행할 것입니다)
examples.suggested: (앞으로도 편할 때는 이렇게 표시하겠습니다)
examples.why: This is stiff, literal translationese. The verb '수행하다' has no clear object here.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: entry 4 keeps all three components (복소수 성분을 갖는 벡터, 고전 정보를 추출할 수 있게 하는 측정, 유니터리 행렬로 기술되는 연산) and the tooltip correctly says the physical details are 추상화, and entry 5 keeps the 단일 시스템 vs. 다중 시스템 contrast, including 서로 상호작용하고 상관관계를 가질 수 있는.

Entry 8 is accurate and won't mislead anyone. All three audience examples are there (학계 교수진, 대기업의 프로젝트 리더, 스타트업 경영진), the "and more" survives as 등, and "particular use to organizations new to quantum computing" is kept as 처음 접하는 조직에 특히 유용할 것입니다. The one issue is register: the entry uses 하십시오체 (권장합니다, 유용할 것입니다) where the project convention is 해요체. That is a minor formal slip. The neighbouring entries use the same formal endings, so fixing the register should cover the whole page, not just this entry.

examples.source: We recommend this course for leaders and architects of quantum initiatives ... It will be of particular use to organizations new to quantum computing.
examples.translation: 이 강좌는 학계 교수진, 대기업의 프로젝트 리더, 스타트업 경영진 등 양자 이니셔티브의 리더와 아키텍트에게 권장합니다. 양자 컴퓨팅을 처음 접하는 조직에 특히 유용할 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 이 강좌는 학계 교수진, 대기업의 프로젝트 리더, 스타트업 경영진 등 양자 이니셔티브를 이끄는 리더와 아키텍트에게 권장해요. 양자 컴퓨팅을 처음 접하는 조직에 특히 유용할 거예요.
examples.why: The meaning is faithful, but the endings are 하십시오체 (권장합니다/것입니다), not the project's 해요체 convention. This is a minor formal-register slip, and the rest of the page has it too.

editor_note: In entry 17, "up to a global phase" became "전역 위상까지 고려했을 때" ("when the global phase is also taken into account"). That says the opposite of the English, which means the global phase is ignored. A learner would read it as claiming that commuting Pauli operations act as logical Paulis even including phase. The rest is minor: entry 17's "사실상 하나의 예제 클래스" is a calque, and "레슨" there clashes with "단원" in entry 5. Entry 12 renders "touches" literally as "접촉하는" and drops "for them" from "building gadgets for them", and entry 45's "특히" is a stiff calque of "In particular".

examples.source: up to a global phase, Pauli operations that commute with every stabilizer generator ... act like Pauli operations
examples.translation: 전역 위상까지 고려했을 때, 안정자 코드의 모든 안정자 생성원과 교환하는 Pauli 연산은 ... Pauli 연산처럼 작동합니다
examples.suggested: 전역 위상 차이를 무시하면, 안정자 코드의 모든 안정자 생성원과 교환하는 Pauli 연산은 ... Pauli 연산처럼 작동합니다
examples.why: '~까지 고려했을 때' means the global phase IS taken into account, which inverts 'up to' (= disregarding). Learners could conclude the equivalence holds exactly, phase included.

examples.source: For a second example — really a class of examples — consider any Pauli gate.
examples.translation: 두 번째 예 — 사실상 하나의 예제 클래스 — 로, 임의의 Pauli 게이트를 생각해 보세요.
examples.suggested: 두 번째 예로(사실은 여러 예를 묶은 하나의 부류로), 임의의 Pauli 게이트를 생각해 보세요.
examples.why: '예제 클래스' is a calque that reads like a programming 'class'. The lesson reference also uses '레슨', while entry 5 uses '단원'.

examples.source: which means building gadgets for them that have a certain simple form ... each code block that it touches
examples.translation: 이는 특정한 단순한 형태를 가진 가젯(gadget)으로 구축하는 것을 의미합니다 ... 접촉하는 각 코드 블록 내의
examples.suggested: 이는 Gate에 대해 특정한 단순한 형태의 가젯(gadget)을 구성한다는 뜻입니다 ... 자신이 작용하는 각 코드 블록 내의
examples.why: The object ('for them' = the gates) is dropped, and '접촉하는' is a literal rendering of 'touches'. '작용하는/관여하는' is what a Korean physicist would write.

examples.source: In particular, the following circuit shows one way to do this.
examples.translation: 특히, 다음 회로는 이를 수행하는 한 가지 방법을 보여줍니다.
examples.suggested: 구체적으로, 다음 회로가 이를 수행하는 한 가지 방법을 보여줍니다.
examples.why: '특히' is a stiff calque of 'In particular' in this sense. '구체적으로' reads more naturally. Meaning is otherwise faithful.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 9 keeps the query-algorithm to factoring/search progression (양자 질의(query) 알고리즘, 개념 증명, 비정형 검색), and entry 17 keeps every privacy caveat, including "전 세계의 IBM 자회사 및 제3자와 공유할 수 있습니다", in the standard 귀하 legal-notice register.

None of the four rewritten entries (36, 61, 98, 107) would mislead a learner. Entry 36 keeps the distinction between the probability of |0^n> and the output bit, entry 98 keeps "1 query versus n queries", and entry 107 keeps the point that ruling out efficient classical approaches is hard. The problems are all in entry 61. The comma after "대칭적인 연산으로" sits inside the math delimiters ("연산으로$,x$와"), so it renders as a math-italic ",x" with no space before it. The connective "같은 말로" is also slightly off-register for "or equivalently"; "또는 동등하게" / "다시 말해" reads more naturally.

examples.source: Notice that this is a symmetric operation, meaning that the result doesn't change if we swap $x$ and $y$
examples.translation: 이 연산은 대칭적인 연산으로$,x$와 $y$를 서로 바꾸어도 결과가 변하지 않으므로
examples.suggested: 이 연산은 대칭적이어서, $x$와 $y$를 서로 바꾸어도 결과가 변하지 않으므로
examples.why: The comma has slipped inside the math delimiters ($,x$), so the text runs straight into a math-italic ',x' with no space. The repeated '연산은 … 연산으로' is also a little clunky.

examples.source: or equivalently, the parity of the bits of $y$ in positions where the string $x$ has a $1$.
examples.translation: 같은 말로, 문자열 $x$에서 $1$인 위치에 해당하는 $y$의 비트들의 패리티로 생각할 수도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 또는 동등하게, 문자열 $x$에서 $1$인 위치에 해당하는 $y$의 비트들의 패리티로 볼 수도 있습니다.
examples.why: '같은 말로' sounds colloquial and slightly odd in a math context. '동등하게' or '다시 말해' is the usual technical connective for 'equivalently'.

editor_note: Entry 22 (유일 탐색, with the promise rendered as *약속*) is faithful and natural. Entry 13's first sentence is accurate, but its second sentence is stiff. The EN dash aside ("we need to make sure that this is possible to do with a unitary quantum operation…") comes out as a clause opening with a second '이것은' and ending in '수행이 가능해야 하는데'. That makes the checking step ("we need to make sure") read as a bare requirement and blurs why the precise treatment is postponed. It does not mislead: the unitary requirement and the superposition queries are both kept. A native editor would still restructure the sentence.

examples.source: The precise way that this works for quantum algorithms will be discussed shortly — we need to make sure that this is possible to do with a unitary quantum operation allowing queries to be made in superposition — but for now we can think about it intuitively at a high level.
examples.translation: 이것이 양자 알고리즘에서 정확히 어떻게 작동하는지는 곧 논의할 것입니다. 이것은 쿼리가 중첩 상태에서 수행될 수 있도록 하는 유니타리 양자 연산으로 수행이 가능해야 하는데, 우선은 큰 틀에서 직관적으로 이해하고 넘어가면 됩니다.
examples.suggested: 양자 알고리즘에서 이것이 정확히 어떻게 작동하는지는 곧 다룹니다. 쿼리를 중첩 상태로 수행할 수 있게 해 주는 유니타리 양자 연산으로 이를 구현할 수 있는지 확인해야 하기 때문입니다. 지금은 큰 틀에서 직관적으로 생각해 보면 됩니다.
examples.why: '이것' is repeated, the '수행…수행이 가능해야 하는데' construction is calqued and stiff, and the sense of 'we need to make sure' (a check still to be done, which is why the details are postponed) is flattened. The meaning is not inverted.

editor_note: Rewritten entries 3 and 5 are faithful to the English. Entry 3 keeps projective measurements as including standard basis measurements (*표준 기저 측정*을 포함한 *사영 측정*) and keeps the hedge "generally" in 일반적으로 ... 변화시키거나 파괴합니다. Entry 5 keeps the key contrasts: "a known collection of states" is 알려진 상태들의 집합, and tomography works from "many independent copies" of "a single, unknown" state (알려지지 않은 어떤 양자 상태 하나에 대해 서로 독립인 사본이 여러 개).

Entry 21 is faithful in every clause: "IBM의 승인을 받아 미국에 소재한 제3자 데이터 처리자인 Credly" keeps the authorization and location, and "전 세계의 IBM 자회사 및 제3자와 공유할 수 있습니다" keeps the hedge in "may"; the formal 귀하/합니다 wording is the standard Korean style for a privacy notice.

Entry 48 is faithful and natural: "오류 완화 옵션에 대한 자세한 내용은 다음 가이드와 API 참조에서 확인할 수 있습니다", and the link label "오류 완화 구성" matches entry 42, with the EstimatorOptions/SamplerOptions API names correctly left in English.

None of the 8 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The rotation amounts in [34] and [58] (5/16, 10/16, 5/8, 10/8→1/4, 20/8→1/2 바퀴), the flip cadence in [28] and the "only if control is |1⟩" condition in [79] all match the English. Two phrasing slips remain. In [34], "그 다음 Qubit은 이것의 두 배(...)이며" has no rotation verb, so it literally says the qubit "is double this". In [73], "한 세트의 Qubit 레지스터에 있습니다" is a stiff calque of "in one set of qubit registers".

examples.source: The next qubit is turned double this ($\tfrac{10}{16}\times 2\pi$ radians, or $10/16$ full turns)
examples.translation: 그 다음 Qubit은 이것의 두 배($\tfrac{10}{16}\times 2\pi$ 라디안, 즉 $10/16$ 바퀴)이며
examples.suggested: 그 다음 Qubit은 이것의 두 배($\tfrac{10}{16}\times 2\pi$ 라디안, 즉 $10/16$ 바퀴)만큼 회전하며
examples.why: The rotation verb is missing, so the sentence literally says the qubit itself 'is double this'. Restoring 회전하며 makes it read naturally.

examples.source: $\vert\psi\rangle$ is in one set of qubit registers.
examples.translation: $\vert\psi\rangle$은 한 세트의 Qubit 레지스터에 있습니다.
examples.suggested: $\vert\psi\rangle$은 하나의 Qubit 레지스터에 준비되어 있습니다.
examples.why: '한 세트의' calques 'one set of'. A Korean technical writer would name the register directly.

editor_note: Entry 4 "양자 프로젝트 설계와 주도" is a faithful, concise course title that renders both "Designing" (설계) and "Leading" (주도), and its noun-pair style matches sibling titles such as "변분 알고리즘 설계" and "양자 정보의 기초".

All four rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally in 해요체: [42] gets the key caveat right ("-" 위상으로 표시되었지만 … 아직 해당 상태의 측정 확률 증가로 이어지지는 않습니다"), [48] keeps both reflection cases ("$|v\rangle$ 방향의 상태는 변하지 않고 … 수직인 상태는 부호가 반전됩니다"), and [61] renders "given that verification is free" correctly as "검증에 비용이 들지 않는다면"; the doubled "$|+\rangle$와 $|+\rangle$" in [32] copies a typo in the English source and is not a translation error.

Both rewritten entries (95 and 116) keep the meaning of the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. That covers the no-cloning claim ("원본을 그대로 보존한 채 … 유니터리 연산은 존재하지 않는다"), the idea that a same-basis measurement is deterministic so one measurement is enough, and the warning to reverse the bit order. Two phrasings in these entries are stiff. In entry 95, "Informally" is rendered literally as "비공식적으로 설명하면", which reads like "unofficially" in Korean; "엄밀하지 않게 말하면" or "간단히 말하면" is the usual way to say it. In entry 116, the modifier phrase in parentheses after the noun ("큐비트(확률적 결과를 가지며 해석을 위해 여러 번의 측정이 필요한)") follows English word order and ends abruptly.

examples.source: Informally, it says that there is no unitary (quantum mechanical) operation that can make a second copy of an arbitrary quantum state
examples.translation: 비공식적으로 설명하면, 원본을 그대로 보존한 채 임의의 양자 상태의 사본을 하나 더 만들어 내는 유니터리(양자역학적) 연산은 존재하지 않는다는 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 엄밀하지 않게 말하면, 원본을 그대로 보존한 채 임의의 양자 상태의 사본을 하나 더 만들어 내는 유니터리(양자역학적) 연산은 존재하지 않는다는 것입니다.
examples.why: In a math context, '비공식적으로' is a literal rendering of 'informally' and sounds like 'unofficially'. Korean technical writers say '엄밀하지 않게 말하면' or '간단히 말하면'.

examples.source: Those qubits with states prepared and measured in different bases (which would have probabilistic outcomes and would require many measurements to interpret) will not be used
examples.translation: 다른 기저로 준비되고 측정된 큐비트(확률적 결과를 가지며 해석을 위해 여러 번의 측정이 필요한)는 일회용 패드/키를 구성하는 데 사용되지 않습니다.
examples.suggested: 다른 기저로 준비되고 측정된 큐비트는 결과가 확률적이어서 해석하려면 여러 번 측정해야 하므로, 일회용 패드/키를 구성하는 데 사용하지 않습니다.
examples.why: The parenthetical copies the English relative clause and ends in a modifier ending ('필요한') that is left hanging. Folding it into the sentence reads more naturally and makes the reason clearer.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 11 and 187 are faithful. The added gloss in 187, "(즉, 가장 오른쪽에 있는)", is correct and helps. Entry 231 ends in the plain 해라체 "포함할 수 있다", which breaks the page's 해요체 register. In entry 132, "두 개의 선으로 표현됩니다" reads as if the diagram, not the two qubits, is shown by the two wires, so the qubit-to-wire mapping comes out slightly blurred.

examples.source: Quantum circuits may include measurement operations that collapse the superposition state into one of the classically allowed states.
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit은 중첩 상태를 고전적으로 허용되는 상태 중 하나로 붕괴시키는 측정 연산을 포함할 수 있다.
examples.suggested: 양자 Circuit에는 중첩 상태를 고전적으로 허용되는 상태 중 하나로 붕괴시키는 측정 연산이 포함될 수 있어요.
examples.why: The 해라체 ending '-수 있다' breaks the page's 해요체 register.

examples.source: This is the first circuit diagram we see with two qubits, which are represented by the two wires.
examples.translation: 이것은 두 Qubit이 등장하는 첫 번째 Circuit 다이어그램으로, 두 개의 선으로 표현됩니다.
examples.suggested: 두 qubit이 등장하는 첫 Circuit 다이어그램으로, 각 qubit은 두 개의 선으로 표현돼요.
examples.why: The relative clause is attached to the diagram, so it no longer clearly says that the wires stand for the qubits. The sentence also mixes 합니다 and 해요 endings.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 5 renders the survey-for-answer-keys condition as "설문을 작성하면, 정답지와 일반 커리큘럼 내 배치 안내가 포함된 노트북 버전을 요청할 수 있습니다", and entry 9 keeps the "though" caveat as "다만 대부분의 노트북은 작성된 그대로 실행하기만 하면 됩니다".
Both rewritten link labels are accurate and consistent with the rest of the page: 54 uses 동적 디커플링, and 55 uses 복원력, which matches 복원력 수준 in entry 15, along with 측정 오류 완화 and 영잡음 외삽법 (ZNE).

Both rewritten entries are faithful: in [17], stabilizer→안정자, MSE→평균 제곱 오차 and the "lower MSE means higher fidelity" direction are all kept, and in [46] entanglement-swapping→얽힘 교환 and the "length-4 path / maximum coverage" wording carry the English meaning exactly.

None of the 11 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. They keep the crossover result (unitary wins at short separations, dynamic wins at long ones), linear versus constant depth scaling, and the fixed measurement cost. In entry 97, "often dominates" became the flat "지배적이며" because the hedge "often" (종종) was dropped, so the claim reads stronger than the English. Entry 89 says "유니터리 방법과 동적 방법 간의 평균값을 계산하여", which calques "compute averages for a comparison between" and makes it sound like one average is taken between the two methods.

examples.source: Increased circuit time from measurement and classical operations often dominates, especially when the control–target separation is small.
examples.translation: 측정 및 고전적 연산으로 인한 Circuit 시간 증가가 지배적이며, 특히 제어-타겟 간 거리가 짧을 때 두드러집니다.
examples.suggested: 측정 및 고전적 연산으로 인한 회로 시간 증가가 종종 지배적인 요인이 되며, 특히 제어-타겟 간 거리가 짧을 때 두드러져요.
examples.why: Dropping 'often' (종종) turns a hedged statement into an absolute one. This is a dropped qualifier, not a misleading error.

examples.source: Running repeated trials allows us to compute averages for a more accurate comparison between the unitary and dynamic methods
examples.translation: 반복 시행을 통해 유니터리(unitary) 방법과 동적(dynamic) 방법 간의 평균값을 계산하여 더 정확한 비교를 할 수 있으며
examples.suggested: 반복 시행으로 평균값을 구하면 유니터리 방법과 동적 방법을 더 정확하게 비교할 수 있으며
examples.why: '방법 간의 평균값' wrongly attaches the 'between' to the averages, as if one average is taken across both methods. The English means each method is averaged over trials and then the two are compared.

editor_note: All 8 rewritten entries (17, 19, 20, 21, 28, 41, 55, 56) say what the English says. The inverse channel is still propagated forward and absorbed into the observable, the comparison with PEC's QPU sampling is kept, and the caveat that on a noiseless simulator the inverse channel is the identity (항등 채널) is intact. There is no drift or hallucinated claim. The only problem is terminology consistency: the rewritten entries write 'Pauli 전파', 'Pauli 채널', 'Pauli-Lindblad' and 'Clifford/비Clifford' in Latin script, while the unchanged rest of the page uses '파울리', '파울리-린드블라드' and '클리퍼드' (entries 65, 72, 106, 125). The same names are now spelled two ways within one file. The rewritten entries also use -습니다 endings, which matches the rest of the page rather than the 해요체 convention.

examples.source: When the noise is described as a Pauli channel (or more generally as a sparse Pauli-Lindblad channel) ... layers of Clifford and non-Clifford operations
examples.translation: 노이즈가 Pauli 채널(또는 더 일반적으로 희소 Pauli-Lindblad 채널)로 기술될 경우 ... Clifford 및 비Clifford 연산의 레이어
examples.suggested: 노이즈가 파울리 채널(또는 더 일반적으로 희소 파울리-린드블라드 채널)로 기술될 경우 ... 클리퍼드 및 비클리퍼드 연산의 레이어
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 파울리, 파울리-린드블라드 and 클리퍼드 (entries 65, 72, 106). The rewrite brings in Latin-script spellings of the same names, so the page is inconsistent.

examples.source: the sparse Pauli-Lindblad noise channel attached to each unique two-qubit layer
examples.translation: 희소 Pauli-Lindblad 노이즈 채널
examples.suggested: 희소 파울리-린드블라드 노이즈 채널
examples.why: Entry 106 renders the same term as 파울리-린드블라드. The rewritten entry is inconsistent with it.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural. Entry 45 renders "with and without OBP" as "OBP 적용 여부에 따른". Entry 47 keeps the contrast between the two modes: "매우 대략적인 추정치… QPU 시간이 필요 없습니다" versus "비교적 정확한 추정값… 몇 분의 QPU 시간을 사용합니다", and the hedged "would potentially reduce" is kept as "줄일 수 있는지".

All six rewritten entries keep the English meaning, and none would mislead a learner. Entry 51's COBYLA noise caveat and its list of causes are intact, entry 35 keeps the note that the "small-scale" example still runs on real hardware with 127 or more qubits, and 56/58/70 use 가장 좋은 컷 consistently with 컷 in entries 59 and 61. The one problem is entry 15, which uses two terms that don't match the rest of the page: it renders max-cut as 최대 절단 where entry 14 set 최대 컷 and every other entry uses max-cut, and it writes 비용 해밀토니안 where every other entry has 비용 Hamiltonian.

examples.source: The max-cut example introduces the process of expressing an objective as a cost Hamiltonian
examples.translation: 최대 절단(max-cut) 예제는 목적 함수를 비용 해밀토니안으로 표현하고
examples.suggested: max-cut 예제는 목적 함수를 비용 Hamiltonian으로 표현하고
examples.why: Entry 14 sets the term as 최대 컷 (max-cut), and the rest of the page uses max-cut and 비용 Hamiltonian. Using 최대 절단 and 해밀토니안 here makes the terms inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Entry [45] gets the setup instruction backwards. The English says to create `.env` with the values shown and replace the credential placeholders inside them with your real key and CRN. The Korean ("자격 증명 자리 표시자를 아래 값으로 교체하세요") says to replace the placeholders with the values below, which would leave the placeholder text in the file. The rest is faithful. Two minor points: the file mixes 워크플로우 ([0]) with 워크플로 (everywhere else) and 클래식 ([19], [21]) with 고전 ([4], [53], [71]), and it is written in 합니다체 instead of the project's 해요체 convention.

examples.source: create a `.env` file next to this notebook with the following values, replacing the credential placeholders.
examples.translation: 이 노트북 옆에 `.env` 파일을 만들고 자격 증명 자리 표시자를 아래 값으로 교체하세요.
examples.suggested: 이 노트북 옆에 아래 값으로 `.env` 파일을 만들고, 자격 증명 자리 표시자는 실제 값으로 바꾸세요.
examples.why: It reverses what gets replaced: the placeholders are in the values below and need to be filled in with the user's own credentials. As translated, the learner would copy the placeholders into the file unchanged.

examples.source: classical compute clusters
examples.translation: 클래식 컴퓨팅 클러스터
examples.suggested: 고전 컴퓨팅 클러스터
examples.why: 'classical' is 클래식 here and in [21] but 고전 in [4], [53] and [71]. It should be 고전 throughout.

examples.source: quantum chemistry workflow
examples.translation: 양자 화학 워크플로우
examples.suggested: 양자 화학 워크플로
examples.why: Every other entry in the file uses 워크플로, so this one is inconsistent.

examples.source: Steps 1–3 introduce the QRMI API by using simple circuits.
examples.translation: 1~3단계에서는 간단한 회로를 사용하여 QRMI API를 소개합니다.
examples.suggested: 1~3단계에서는 간단한 회로를 사용해 QRMI API를 소개해요.
examples.why: The whole file uses 합니다체 (-습니다/-합니다), but the project convention is 해요체.

editor_note: Five of the six rewritten entries (15, 44, 46, 54, 66) are faithful and read naturally. That includes the deep-circuit/lattice-model trade-off and the provable-convergence caveat "적절한 가정 하에서" in [15], the three-electrons-into-4-modes / seven XXPlusYYGate description in [46], and the consistent use of 휴리스틱 변분 앤자츠. The one slip is word order in [36]. "SQD로 결합된 비트열 집합을 후처리합니다" puts "SQD로" right before "결합된", so it can read as "the bitstring set combined by SQD", when the English says the combined set is post-processed with SQD. Moving "SQD로" next to the verb fixes this.

examples.source: we will sample from this set of circuits and post-process the combined set of bitstrings with SQD
examples.translation: 이 Circuit 집합에서 샘플링하고 SQD로 결합된 비트열 집합을 후처리합니다
examples.suggested: 이 Circuit 집합에서 샘플링한 뒤, 결합된 비트열 집합을 SQD로 후처리합니다
examples.why: Because 'SQD로' comes right before '결합된', it attaches to that word and suggests SQD does the combining. In the English, SQD is the post-processing tool.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (70, 71, 74, 76) would mislead a learner. The arithmetic (3% of 40,000 is about 1,200), the two-job count, the tags and the tradeoffs (fewer checks or less depth raise the rate; shots scale with the inverse of the rate) are all intact, and 반영 for "commit" stays consistent with the rest of the page. Two phrasings in these entries still read stiff. In entry 70, "모든 엣지가 동일하게 노이즈가 있다고 가정하는" is a literal calque of "every edge is equally noisy". In entry 71, "3%의 비율에서는 40,000샷이 … 샘플을 남깁니다" makes the shots the subject of 남기다, which reads like English syntax.

examples.source: rather than assuming every edge is equally noisy
examples.translation: 모든 엣지가 동일하게 노이즈가 있다고 가정하는 대신
examples.suggested: 모든 엣지의 노이즈가 같다고 가정하는 대신
examples.why: '동일하게 노이즈가 있다' is a word-for-word rendering of 'equally noisy'. A Korean technical writer would compare the noise levels directly.

examples.source: at a 3% rate, 40,000 shots leave roughly 1,200 postselected samples per circuit
examples.translation: 3%의 비율에서는 40,000샷이 회로당 약 1,200개의 사후 선택된 샘플을 남깁니다
examples.suggested: 사후 선택률이 3%라면 40,000샷을 실행해도 회로당 사후 선택된 샘플은 약 1,200개만 남습니다
examples.why: With shots as the subject of 남기다, the sentence follows English syntax. '3%의 비율' also drops the referent (the postselection rate), which the suggestion restores.

editor_note: Entry 8 is faithful and natural: "이 워크플로에서 사용되는 [Sampler] 프리미티브 사용 방법" keeps Sampler in English, uses the standard term 프리미티브, and correctly attaches the "used in this workflow" clause to the primitive as a prerequisite item.

Entry 81 is accurate. Control |0⟩ applies the identity (no operation), control |1⟩ applies X to the target, and the closing point that CNOT is limited to classical operations when both inputs are classical states is kept. The one thing a native editor would change is the opening phrase "두 Qubit의 대표적인 Gate". It reads as "the representative gate of two qubits", a calque of "canonical two qubit gate", and it clashes with "2-qubit Gate" in the next sentence. "대표적인 2-qubit Gate" is the natural wording and matches the rest of the entry.

examples.source: We start with the canonical two qubit gate, the controlled-NOT (also CNOT or CX) gate.
examples.translation: 두 Qubit의 대표적인 Gate인 controlled-NOT(CNOT 또는 CX) Gate부터 시작합니다.
examples.suggested: 대표적인 2-qubit Gate인 controlled-NOT(CNOT 또는 CX) Gate부터 시작합니다.
examples.why: '두 Qubit의 대표적인 Gate' is a calque that reads as 'the representative gate of two qubits' and doesn't match '2-qubit Gate' in the next sentence. The meaning is not changed.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (48, 55, 73) would mislead a learner. Entry 48 keeps the "might approach or exceed T2" hedge, and entry 55 renders controllability as 제어 가능성 and control knobs as 제어 수단 correctly. Entry 73 has two small problems a native editor would fix. Its last sentence has a dangling subject: "Qiskit을 사용하면 … 시뮬레이션할 수 있어, … 개념적 모델을 제공합니다" doesn't say what provides the model. Its first sentence is a calque, "마스터함으로써 … 이해하게 되며, 이는 … 토대를 마련합니다", and the hypothetical "would be created" became a flat statement (생성됩니다). The 합니다체 register matches the rest of the page.

examples.source: Qiskit allows us to simulate the protocol's logic perfectly, providing a conceptual model for how these criteria are met in communication architectures.
examples.translation: Qiskit을 사용하면 이 프로토콜의 논리를 완벽하게 시뮬레이션할 수 있어, 통신 아키텍처에서 이러한 기준들이 어떻게 충족되는지에 대한 개념적 모델을 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: Qiskit으로 이 프로토콜의 논리를 완벽하게 시뮬레이션할 수 있으며, 이는 통신 아키텍처에서 이러한 기준들이 어떻게 충족되는지 보여 주는 개념적 모델이 됩니다.
examples.why: The subject of 제공합니다 is never stated. The conditional clause 'Qiskit을 사용하면' can't serve as the subject of the main verb, so the sentence reads as machine-translated.

examples.source: By mastering quantum teleportation, you'll understand how to encode, transmit, and recover quantum information between distinct nodes—laying the foundation for ...
examples.translation: 양자 순간이동을 마스터함으로써, 서로 다른 노드 간에 양자 정보를 인코딩하고, 전송하고, 복구하는 방법을 이해하게 되며, 이는 ... 토대를 마련합니다.
examples.suggested: 양자 순간이동을 익히면 서로 다른 노드 사이에서 양자 정보를 인코딩·전송·복원하는 방법을 이해하게 되고, 이것이 ... 토대가 됩니다.
examples.why: The '마스터함으로써 … 이며, 이는' structure copies the English sentence shape. A Korean technical writer would use '익히면' and a simpler clause chain.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries misleads a learner. In [34], the claim that continuous re-initialization is an active research topic because doing it quickly is hard ("빠르게 수행하기 어렵기 때문에") is kept, and so is the X-gate example. In [36], T₁ and T₂ are rendered correctly as 에너지 이완 시간 and 위상 결어긋남 시간, with "훨씬 초과해야" for "greatly exceed". In [52], control knobs becomes 제어 수단 for controllability, which is fine. The one thing to change is the sign-off in [79]: "즐거운 양자 컴퓨팅 되세요!" copies the "즐거운 하루 되세요" greeting pattern onto an activity, and a native editor would rewrite it.

examples.source: Feel free to extend these experiments, and happy quantum computing!
examples.translation: 이 실험들을 자유롭게 확장해 보면서 즐거운 양자 컴퓨팅 되세요!
examples.suggested: 이 실험들을 자유롭게 확장해 보면서 양자 컴퓨팅을 즐겨 보세요!
examples.why: '즐거운 X 되세요' fits time spans such as a day or a weekend. It does not fit an activity like 양자 컴퓨팅, so the line reads as a literal copy of 'happy quantum computing'.
